about.title: San Juan Capistrano Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: San Juan Capistrano's mix of historic downtown, equestrian trails, and busy corridors like I-5 and Del Obispo Street means residents rely daily on vehicles, tools, appliances, and recreational gear. When one of those products fails because of a flaw in its design, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning label, the consequences can be serious. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers without having to prove anyone was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. If you were injured by a faulty product anywhere in San Juan Capistrano, from a malfunctioning car part to a defective household item, it helps to have someone review what happened and explain your options. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can look at your situation and advise on next steps. Keeping the product itself, along with packaging and receipts, can matter a great deal to any potential claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rules, you generally only need to show the product was defective and caused your injury, not that a company was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: Preserving the Product Can Be Critical
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any related paperwork intact can help an attorney evaluate what went wrong and build your case.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and caused your injury, not that the company acted carelessly. An independent attorney can review your specific facts and confirm how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, manuals, or receipts. This evidence can be important for evaluating a design, manufacturing, or warning defect. Avoid repairing or discarding it before speaking with an attorney.
